title: Mobile Safari momentum scrolling & Firefox form-control visual regressions triage
creator: Liam Patel
description:
Summary: During the last QA sweep we observed multiple visual and interaction regressions that surface primarily on iOS Safari (momentum/overscroll, toucharea misalignment) and Firefox desktop (native form-control rendering, subpixel chart anti-aliasing). Affects tokens, primary/secondary buttons, table sticky headers with virtualized lists, and SVG-based charts. This ticket captures triage, reproduction, and proposed remediation tasks for design + engineering to prioritize before the 2026.03 UI Kit release.

Components impacted: tokens (spacing & background bleed on overscroll), buttons (height & focus ring misalignment in Firefox), tables (sticky header overlap when virtualization inserts container transforms), charts (SVG path blur at fractional devicePixelRatio), form elements (Firefox selects/textareas using UA styles that break compact layouts).

Reproduction notes (representative):
1) iPhone 14 / iOS 16+ / Safari: open Dashboard > Recent Sessions table (virtualized). Scroll quickly to the bottom and perform a momentum flick. Observed: background token colors briefly exposed at container edges, and sticky header jumps causing row overlap. Screenshot: attached.
2) macOS Ventura / Firefox 110+: open Settings > Integrations > Add API Key button. Focus button via keyboard (Tab). Observed: Firefox default focus ring pushes button content down ~1px and halves visual alignment with labels. Also native select appearance differs from Chromium and causes layout shifts in compact forms.
3) Chrome (stable) / Android: not a blocker but verify parity for touch target sizing.
4) Charts: line charts with small stroke widths render with fuzzy edges at DPR 1.5 on Safari due to subpixel transforms applied by our chart wrapper.

Immediate triage decisions:
- Prioritize safety fixes that prevent content overlap (tables/sticky headers) and button hit-target regressions.
- Token bleed during overscroll: implement containment clip + background-color propagation (design to confirm token backgrounds to use layer tokens with same painting order). Engineering to prototype overflow clipping and check performance on iOS.
- Firefox focus ring: opt for an explicit focus outline style in UI Kit that normalizes across browsers (outline-offset and box-shadow fallback). Design will provide exact spec tokens.
- Charts: force pixel-aligned rendering for critical small-stroke charts by rounding transform values in the chart wrapper; add a regression test in Percy/Screenshot harness.

Proposed tasks (split between Design and Eng):
- Design: publish updated focus token (focus-compact, focus-regular) and provide examples for buttons/forms in Figma file.
- Eng: ENG-4521 + ENG-4599 to implement sticky-header z-index/transform fixes and chart wrapper rounding. Add automated e2e tests in BrowserStack reagents for iOS Safari momentum scenarios.
- QA: create a focused test plan for the top-10 affected screens; capture video of momentum flick repro, and add to the release checklist.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sticky headers no longer overlap rows during momentum/fast-scrolling on iOS Safari (verified on device).
- Buttons have consistent visual focus and height across Chromium, Firefox, and Safari (keyboard and touch).
- Charts render crisp strokes at DPR 1.0/1.5/2.0 in Safari and Firefox (pixel-comparison < 2% diff on key frames).
- New design tokens and focus styles published to the UI Kit and linked in the changelog.

Notes about scope: This ticket intentionally avoids deep rework of the virtualization strategy — we want minimal, low-risk fixes first (clipping and z-index/transform normalization). If issues persist after these fixes, open a follow-up ENG ticket to re-evaluate virtualization integration with sticky headers.
acceptance_criteria: No row overlap during iOS Safari momentum scrolling on verified devices
Buttons show identical height and focus treatment across Chrome/Firefox/Safari
SVG charts baseline frames match approved goldens at DPR 1.0/1.5/2.0
Design tokens published and referenced in release notes
